reason: BFI National Archive's online catalogue (collections-search.bfi.org.uk, an Axiell/Adlib 'AIS' platform) DOES expose in-scope flat-art databases — ChoicePosters ('Posters and Designs'), ChoiceStills ('Stills'), ChoiceArchive ('Scripts, Documents and Ephemera') — alongside the dominant moving-image ChoiceFilmWorks (BFI's own help cites 'over 800,000 film titles'). A simple-search for 'Hitchcock' scoped to those flat-art DBs returns real counts (654 Posters + 5 Stills via the per-database refine links), so the metadata catalogue is substantial. BUT there is no public machine-readable source that serves downloadable in-scope images >=600px on BFI's own infra, for two independent, decisive reasons: (1) IMAGE DELIVERY IS INTERNAL-ONLY. The collection viewer's own JS (/web/Scripts/Base/ImageViewer.js -> /web/helper/GetImageURL) returns the image URL template 'http://api-public-ext.bfihosting.com/wwwopacx/wwwopac.ashx?command=getcontent&server=images&value={filename}&width=600&height=600'. That host, api-public-ext.bfihosting.com, is NXDOMAIN on public DNS (confirmed via Google 8.8.8.8 AND Cloudflare 1.1.1.1) — it is an internal/on-premise hostname not reachable from the public internet. The public collections-search host does NOT reverse-proxy getcontent (collections-search.bfi.org.uk/wwwopacx/... = HTTP 404; /web/Output/wwwopac.ashx?command=getcontent = 302 -> /web/error). (2) THE RECORD-DRILL SUBSYSTEM IS BROKEN. The site carries a live banner ('We are aware that some users are experiencing technical difficulties with Collections Search') and in practice every path from the results overview into an actual record fails: /web/results/{N}, /web/Details/{db}/{N}, and the per-DB 'Search'/'Refine' actions (/web/search/simple/repeat, /web/search/simple/refine) all 302 -> /web/error?aspxerrorpath=... So even the per-record metadata + ais-image-filename needed to build a getcontent URL cannot be reached anonymously. (3) AUTHORITATIVE CONFIRMATION OF ON-SITE-ONLY ACCESS. BFI's own guidance (and a corroborating web result for the Collections Search) states digitised images are viewable on-site only: 'you won't be able to view actual digitised images unless at a BFI site'. The BFI National Archive Special Collections / Screencraft page confirms most Screencraft material (posters, designs, scripts, stills) is non-digitised, requires in-person research appointments in Berkhamsted, and 'we do not have a digitisation on-demand service.' Net: in-scope flat film art (posters/stills/designs) exists as catalogue metadata but the images are firewalled behind an internal image host + on-site access, and the record-detail navigation is currently non-functional. Fails the film-museum scope gate (no downloadable flat-art images >=600px on the museum's own public infra).
easy_source_found: No. Stage-0 checks all negative: collections-search.bfi.org.uk and www.bfi.org.uk /opendata|/api|/developers|/data|/api/v1 = 404; data.bfi.org.uk, collections.bfi.org.uk = NXDOMAIN; no Drupal /jsonapi, eMuseum, CONTENTdm, Solr, IIIF presentation API, _next/data, or GraphQL on the collection host. The bfidatadigipres GitHub org exists but holds only IIIF *infrastructure* (bfi_universal_viewer fork, bfi-iiif-load-balancer, bfi-iiif-auth-shim, bfi-iiif-logging) and DPX/encoding/checksum tooling — no collection data dump, and the IIIF stack is auth-shimmed (not an anonymous open-image API). The only programmatic surface is the Adlib wwwopac.ashx getcontent image resizer, which lives on the non-public host api-public-ext.bfihosting.com (NXDOMAIN).
probe_summary: Identified the platform (Axiell/Adlib AIS) and the in-scope databases (ChoicePosters 'Posters and Designs', ChoiceStills 'Stills', ChoiceArchive). Reproduced a working simple-search via session POST to /web/search/simple -> 302 /web/results: 'Hitchcock' yields 654 Posters + 5 Stills (counts only, on the results-overview page). Could NOT reach any individual record: results-drill endpoints (/web/results/N, /web/Details/db/N, /web/search/simple/repeat, /web/search/simple/refine) all 302 to /web/error (site shows a 'technical difficulties' banner). Decoded image delivery from ImageViewer.js: /web/helper/GetImageURL returns {"Url":"http://api-public-ext.bfihosting.com/wwwopacx/wwwopac.ashx?command=getcontent&server=images&value=...&width=600&height=600"} — but that host is NXDOMAIN on public DNS (8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1), and the public collections-search host does not proxy getcontent. No downloadable flat-art image >=600px obtainable; BFI documentation confirms digitised images are on-site-only.

exhibitions_entry.name: BFI National Archive
exhibitions_entry.description: Founded in 1935, the BFI National Archive is one of the largest and oldest film and television archives in the world, holding over a million moving-image titles. Alongside its film holdings it preserves the BFI's Special Collections (Screencraft) — film posters, production stills and photographs, set and costume designs, animation drawings, scripts, storyboards and pressbooks — documenting the off-screen craft of cinema. While its Collections Search catalogue is available online, the digitised images of stills, posters and designs can generally be consulted only on-site, with most Screencraft material held at the archive's research centre in Berkhamsted, Hertfordshire and viewable by appointment.
exhibitions_entry.description_ko: 1935년에 설립된 BFI 국립영화아카이브는 세계에서 가장 크고 오래된 영화·텔레비전 아카이브 가운데 하나로, 100만 점이 넘는 무빙이미지 작품을 소장하고 있다. 필름 외에도 BFI의 특별 컬렉션인 '스크린크래프트(Screencraft)'를 보존하는데, 영화 포스터·제작 스틸 사진·세트 및 의상 디자인·애니메이션 드로잉·시나리오·스토리보드·홍보 책자 등 스크린 너머 영화 제작의 손길이 담긴 자료들이다. 온라인 컬렉션 검색 카탈로그는 공개되어 있지만, 스틸·포스터·디자인의 디지털 이미지는 대체로 현장에서만 열람할 수 있으며, 스크린크래프트 자료 대부분은 허트퍼드셔주 버컴스테드의 아카이브 연구센터에 보관되어 예약을 통해서만 볼 수 있다.

notes: Start URL https://collections-search.bfi.org.uk/web works (200) — the bare domain root is a default IIS page, the app lives under /web. Reusable recipe if revisited: session is required (ASP.NET_SessionId set on GET /web/search/simple); search = POST /web/search/simple with DatabaseChoices[0..7].Name/.Selected (ChoiceFilmWorks,ChoiceBooks,ChoiceSerials,ChoiceArticles,ChoicePresscuttings,ChoiceArchive,ChoicePosters,ChoiceStills) + Fields[0].FieldName=Search_SearchSimple_FieldLabel & Fields[0].Value=<q>; on success it 302s to /web/results (results-overview with per-DB counts). RECONSIDER only if BFI (a) fixes the broken record-drill subsystem AND (b) exposes the wwwopac.ashx getcontent image host on a PUBLIC, anonymous endpoint (currently api-public-ext.bfihosting.com = internal/NXDOMAIN), or publishes an open-data/IIIF export of Special Collections imagery. As of the probe date (2026-06-16) all in-scope flat-art images are on-site-only per BFI's own access policy, mirroring the cinematheque-fr and deutsche-kinemathek outcomes. Coordinates = BFI Reuben Library / BFI Stephen Street, 21 Stephen St, London W1T 1LN (the public-facing Collections Search access point); the physical Special Collections research centre is in Berkhamsted, Hertfordshire.
